title: A joint statement by the Lean and Mathlib communities says "we have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct" (Lean community blog)
title_en: A joint statement by the Lean and Mathlib communities says "we have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct" (Lean community blog)
author: Lean community blog
content_snippet:
Joint statement by the Lean and Mathlib communities, endorsed by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative.

On November 20, 2026, Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis as a Lean library comprising 17 million lines of code.

We have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct, and we congratulate him on this achievement.

The codebase depends directly only on Mathlib. Over the past day, the Lean and Mathlib communities have rallied to verify the proo
summary_en: Mathematician Levent Alpöge released a formal proof of the Riemann Hypothesis on November 20, 2026, consisting of 17 million lines of Lean code relying on the Mathlib library. The Lean and Mathlib communities have officially certified the proof's correctness after comprehensive verification of its logic and codebase.

content_snippet: Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro demand more for equipment, with the increased costs hitting trading firms
summary_en: Global data center equipment suppliers are significantly increasing prices for previously contracted AI servers, with hikes reaching up to 45%. This surge is driven by extreme supply-demand imbalances in AI infrastructure, forcing manufacturers to bypass existing contract terms to pass on rising memory and component costs.
title_zh: AI服务器供应吃紧，供应商违约提价达45%
summary_zh: 受AI基础设施需求激增驱动，部分供应商在签署供货协议后将服务器价格调涨高达45%

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 全球数据中心设备供应商正大规模上调已签约订单的AI服务器价格，涨幅最高达45%。这一现象源于AI算力基础设施的供需失衡，导致内存及核心服务器组件成本传导效应加剧，进而引发厂商突破既有合同履约义务进行溢价交付。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Global data center equipment suppliers are significantly increasing prices for previously contracted AI servers, with hikes reaching up to 45%. This surge is driven by extreme supply-demand imbalances in AI infrastructure, forcing manufacturers to bypass existing contract terms to pass on rising memory and component costs.

fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】数据中心设备供应商；Nvidia系AI服务器买方在全球数据中心硬件供应链：在合同签订后强行将AI服务器售价上调至多45%

fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Data center equipment suppliers; Buyers of Nvidia-powered AI servers: Unilaterally increasing AI server prices by up to 45% post-contract
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Explosive demand for AI compute infrastructure and upstream memory shortages squeezing supplier margins
[Key Metrics] 45% price hike post-contract, shift in supply chain bargaining power.
[Industry Impact & Outlook] Market impact: Transition from budget-driven to supply-security-driven compute procurement.

title: The UN fails to agree on rules regulating ‘killer robots’
title_en: The UN fails to agree on rules regulating ‘killer robots’
author: Terrence O'Brien
content_snippet:
One of the items on the agenda for UN diplomats meeting in Geneva this week was working towards rules regarding the use of autonomous weapons, or so-called “killer robots.” Eventually, representatives left the meetings agreeing to “start discussing options” after a largely fruitless week of negotiations.

The compromise reached was that countries would instead have two years to propose regulations. Negotiations between countries on which regulations to adopt and how to enforce them will likely d
summary_en: UN diplomats failed to establish a legally binding framework for lethal autonomous weapons systems at the Geneva meeting, settling only on a two-year window to discuss potential regulatory options. Led by Russia, Israel, and the United States, significant resistance has stalled progress on defining enforceable compliance standards.
title_zh: 联合国自主武器管制谈判进展停滞
summary_zh: 联合国日内瓦会议未能就致命性自主武器系统监管达成共识，仅承诺在未来两年内继续探讨监管框架方案

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 联合国各国外交官在日内瓦会议上试图就规范致命性自主武器系统（Killer Robots）达成协议，但最终未能形成法律约束性框架，仅达成未来两年内提交监管方案的初步共识。以俄罗斯、以色列和美国为代表的国家在磋商中持保守态度，导致关于强制性监管和合规执行的实质性议题陷入长期僵局。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: UN diplomats failed to establish a legally binding framework for lethal autonomous weapons systems at the Geneva meeting, settling only on a two-year window to discuss potential regulatory options. Led by Russia, Israel, and the United States, significant resistance has stalled progress on defining enforceable compliance standards.

fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】联合国各成员国代表、俄罗斯、以色列、美国在瑞士日内瓦联合国裁军相关会议：未能签署监管协议，仅达成未来两年内讨论监管方案的折中意见
【起因与机理】主要军事强国对自主武器技术发展的战略控制权博弈以及对强制性合规的排斥
【核心事实细节】未能签署具强制力的法律文书，仅达成两年期方案讨论延期。
【各方立场与态度】半自主武器与无人机在乌克兰、加沙等地区的使用频率增加与平民伤亡引发人道争议。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] UN member state representatives, Russia, Israel, US (UN meetings in Geneva): Failed to reach a binding agreement, agreeing only to a two-year timeframe for further discussion
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Strategic control over autonomous military technology and resistance to mandatory compliance mechanisms
[Regulatory & Investigation Focus] Failure to produce a legally binding treaty; agreement limited to a two-year consultation period.
[Key Position & Outlook] Rising humanitarian concerns due to increased use of semi-autonomous systems and drones in ongoing global conflicts.

The Chinese businesswoman romantically linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had connections to a network for supplying AI chips that included an alleged Cambodian criminal enterprise, an FT investigation has found.

Former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang is at the centre of US investigations into whether Nvidia’s largest client in south-east Asia was involved in the underground chip trade. Some US officials suspect Alice Huang was a Chinese spy, a claim Beijing dismissed as a “smear”.

title: Amazon closes in on $7.5bn deal to buy AI start-up Decart

author: Oliver Barnes, Ivan Levingston, and Rafe Rosner-Uddin
content_snippet:
Amazon is nearing a $7.5bn deal to buy start-up Decart, underscoring the appetite of technology giants to bolster their AI capabilities.

The potential acquisition of Decart, whose main software product allows AI models to run more efficiently which frees up computer chip capacity, would help Amazon Web Services in its efforts to compete with Nvidia.

Talks were at an advanced stage over a deal valuing Decart at about $7.5bn, according to people familiar with the matter. A deal could come togeth

title: Nvidia researchers argue huge AI context windows are a dead end
title_en: Nvidia researchers argue huge AI context windows are a dead end
author: Jonathan Kemper
content_snippet:
Language models can now process entire novels at once. An Nvidia research team says that's often overkill and expensive. In many tests, periodic summaries and targeted lookups worked about as well.

A language model's context window is its working memory, covering everything it holds in view when generating a reply. Over the past few years, that window has grown rapidly. GPT-4 launched in March 2023 with 8,192 tokens. Today, GPT 5.6 Sol handles around one million tokens, about 120 times as much
summary_en: Nvidia researchers demonstrated that blindly scaling context windows to million-token levels is not the optimal path for LLM efficiency. Their findings indicate that combining periodic summarization with targeted information retrieval achieves comparable performance while significantly reducing computational costs and inference latency.
subheadings: Continue reading with THE DECODER+
title_zh: 英伟达研究指出超长上下文模型非最优解
summary_zh: 英伟达研究团队提出，超长上下文窗口存在冗余，定期摘要与目标检索机制在效率上优于单纯堆叠Token容量

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 英伟达研究团队通过对比实验发现，将上下文窗口盲目扩张至百万级Token并非提升大模型性能的最优路径。研究结果显示，采用定期总结技术与针对性的信息检索方案，在保持任务完成质量的前提下，能显著降低计算资源消耗与推理延迟。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Nvidia researchers demonstrated that blindly scaling context windows to million-token levels is not the optimal path for LLM efficiency. Their findings indicate that combining periodic summarization with targeted information retrieval achieves comparable performance while significantly reducing computational costs and inference latency.

fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】英伟达（Nvidia）研究团队在AI架构性能研究实验：论证超长上下文窗口存在计算冗余，推广定期摘要与检索方案
【起因与机理】应对大模型推理成本高企，探索更高效的内存与计算资源调度方案
【关键技术规格】指出无节制扩展上下文窗口存在高成本冗余。
【各方立场与态度】引导行业关注计算效率与推理成本的平衡优化。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Nvidia research team (AI architectural performance study): Argue against infinite context windows in favor of summarization and retrieval
[Root Cause & Mechanism] To address high inference costs and optimize memory/compute resource allocation
[Key Technical Spec] Identified overhead and high costs in indefinite context window scaling.
[Key Position & Outlook] Advocating for a focus on computational efficiency and cost-balanced model design.

title: Silicon Valley's growing obsession with AI doomsday is turning parts of the tech industry toward cult-like devotion
title_en: Silicon Valley's growing obsession with AI doomsday is turning parts of the tech industry toward cult-like devotion
author: Manuel Uth
content_snippet:
A Buddhist monastery in Vermont wants to become the official church of the AI industry, or, as New Yorker writer Sam Kriss puts it, "a Scientology for Silicon Valley."

Publicly, the group known as Maple promises to save humanity from an AI apocalypse. Behind closed doors, former members say, it records every breath its residents take to build an AI god modeled on its leader's mind. That promise of salvation holds particular appeal for the people who build AI and the infrastructure behind it.

S
summary_en: Maple, founded in 2011 by Soryu Forall, is infiltrating Silicon Valley's AI engineering and data center management workforce through a narrative of AI apocalyptic salvation. Former members report that the organization imposes strict behavioral surveillance to harvest data for training an AI deity modeled after Forall's consciousness, currently generating up to $1 million in annual revenue.
subheadings: Maple's answer to "dataism"puts residents under strict control
Former members say the recordings would train an AI modeled on Forall
Former members report manipulation and psychological breakdowns
Why developers from sensitive fields drift into doomsday cults
Jacob Coxon's Anthropic exit shows how widespread extinction fears are among AI researchers

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 由Soryu Forall于2011年创立的Maple组织（地球生命保存僧院），正通过以“AI末日救赎”为核心的叙事，深度渗透硅谷AI工程师与数据中心管理人员群体。该组织被前成员披露实施严密行为监控，旨在收集个体数据以构建基于其领袖思维模式的AI实体，目前年收入已达100万美元级别。

Former members report that the organization imposes strict behavioral surveillance to harvest data for training an AI deity modeled after Forall's consciousness, currently generating up to $1 million in annual revenue.

author: Sui-Lee Wee and Li You
content_snippet:
As the United States and China vie for artificial intelligence supremacy, Chinese tech companies are facing a mounting challenge: finding the money to keep up.

Like their American rivals, China’s A.I. start-ups face soaring costs to train increasingly powerful models. But while Anthropic raised more than $80 billion in a record-breaking initial public offering this week, its Chinese competitors face a far more unforgiving financial landscape.

Venture capital investment in China lags far behind
summary_en: Chinese tech giants and AI startups are facing severe capital expenditure pressure, with total spending projected to reach $139 billion this year while AI-related revenue covers less than 8%. Beyond U.S. export controls on advanced chips, new regulations are closing loopholes involving Southeast Asian data centers, further exacerbating the mismatch between high CAPEX and insufficient commercial returns.

For almost a decade, a Google lab in Santa Barbara, Calif., has led the global race to build a computer that harnesses the power of quantum mechanics: the unseen physical properties that allow light, subatomic particles and other exotic matter to behave in ways that defy common sense.

title: SpaceX’s subsidiary Cursor tells lawmakers it's considering phasing out Chinese AI models
title_en: SpaceX’s subsidiary Cursor tells lawmakers it's considering phasing out Chinese AI models
author: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
content_snippet:
SpaceX's artificial-intelligence coding platform, Cursor, is considering moving away from using of Chinese AI models due to "geopolitical risk,"CNBC has learned.

Cursor, which SpaceX acquired at an implied $60 billion equity value in August, had built its coding model Composer 2 on top of Chinese lab Moonshot AI's Kimi K2.5.

It's among the U.S. firms that have adopted Chinese models, whose usage has spiked across the globe this year, worrying lawmakers in Washington. The battle for AI supremac
summary_en: SpaceX's AI coding platform, Cursor, informed the U.S. House Committee on Homeland Security and the Select Committee on China that it is exploring the phase-out of the Kimi K2.5 model from Chinese lab Moonshot AI due to geopolitical risks. Investigations revealed that several U.S. firms adopted Chinese models for cost and performance advantages, prompting lawmakers to propose a national American open-weight AI initiative to reduce reliance on foreign models.

author: Artificial Analysis
content_snippet:
Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Mini at 20 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, an open weights looped transformer on the Pareto frontier for Intelligence vs. Active Parameters

Inkling 2 Mini is a 26B total, 5.4B active parameter mixture-of-experts model. The 5.4B active parameter count includes three passes through its looped layers; it uses 3.1B unique weights per text token, and it is small enough to run on a MacBook or DGX Spark.

It is released under an Apache 2.0 licens

title: Many Etsy Sellers Close Up Shop Over Site’s New A.I. Policy
title_en: Many Etsy Sellers Close Up Shop Over Site’s New A.I. Policy
author: Reggie Ugwu
content_snippet:
Many longtime owners of shops on Etsy, the online marketplace known for its handmade goods, said this week that they had left the site over a policy change that they said leaves them vulnerable to exploitation by artificial intelligence companies.

summary_en: Etsy has introduced new terms of service, effective December 16, allowing the company and its third-party partners to use seller content for training and testing AI models. This prompted widespread backlash and shop closures from creators, despite claims from James Ossman, VP of customer operations, that data use is restricted to fraud detection and advertising, as users remain concerned about the lack of opt-out mechanisms and potential IP exploitation.

title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.

author: Dan Goodin
content_snippet:
Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve.

summary_en: HD Moore, Chief Research Officer at Dragos, uncovered major security flaws in the AI supply chain by injecting 2 million trackable 'canary' secrets into AI prompts sent via routing services. title: OpenAI makes it much harder for attackers to extract how its latest AI models think
title_en: OpenAI makes it much harder for attackers to extract how its latest AI models think
author: Matthias Bastian
content_snippet:
OpenAI has sharply tightened safeguards against extracting internal reasoning from GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. Attacks on active requests fell from 22.9 to 0.9 percent, OpenAI says. The company is now bringing selected improvements to GPT-6 Astra, too.

The defenses work on two levels. For individual requests, the systems
summary_en: OpenAI has deployed layered security mechanisms for GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol models, reducing the success rate of black-box inference-extraction attacks from 54% to under 0.2% through targeted training, input/output filtering, and API access restrictions. These measures are designed to neutralize distillation attacks that attempt to reconstruct core reasoning paths, supplemented by the weekly suspension of tens of thousands of illicit accounts.

author: Grace Huckins
content_snippet:

summary_en: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed during their meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen that humans must maintain control over military decisions involving artificial intelligence, prohibiting autonomous 'superintelligence' (SI) in major military actions, as confirmed by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. summary_en: OpenAI has deployed enhanced safeguards to mitigate adversarial distillation, focusing on protecting Chain-of-thought and intermediate reasoning traces. 周四的尾盘走势回吐了 17% 的首日涨幅，为纳斯达克指数下跌 2.2% 提供了难得的亮点。随着人工智能交易的暴跌，大盘继续呈下跌趋势，进入亚洲交易日，全球股市将出现三年多以来最长的连续下跌。
虽然 Claude 聊天机器人开发商在开盘时的强劲表现反映了经历严重超额认购后投资者的巨大热情，但尾盘的回落凸显了大型科技企业面临的市场波动——在企业级软件商业化变现与庞大资本开支周期的交织下，市场情绪正经历剧烈博弈。
Anthropic 将 IPO 发行价定为每股 83 美元，高于此前已上调的指导区间上限，单笔募资超 81 亿美元。在亚马逊（Amazon.com Inc.）与 Alphabet Inc. 等科技巨头的巨额注资背书下，Anthropic 已与 OpenAI 并列成为全球生成式 AI 基础设施的核心支柱。
Anthropic 的挂牌交易引发了华尔街投行的全方位审视，分析师聚焦于前沿大模型研发与 GPU 算力集群的庞大资本开支能否转化为可持续的盈利能力。此次上市创下了全球风险投资支持科技企业史上规模最大的 IPO 纪录，打破了此前所有云计算与移动互联网巨头保持的公开发行市值高度。

paragraphs_zh: 随着通往通用超级人工智能（ASI）的多种技术路径逐步成型，后 AGI 时代的研究范式正从哲学思辨迅速转变为实证科学与系统性治理课题。
数十年来，全球人工智能学术与工业界始终聚焦于一座里程碑：构建通用人工智能（AGI）——即在几乎所有认知任务上均能与人类智力匹敌的智能系统。在原理上，智能超越人类心智极限是必然演进，但由于 AGI 曾被视作遥不可及且充满巨大不确定性，跨越它去探讨更远未来曾显得为时过早。
然而，当 AGI 已清晰步入人类视野与现实技术射程之内，我们再也无法推迟对“AGI 之后”的严肃审视。AI 极有可能以现有惊人节奏持续演进，甚至开启加速正反馈，向通用超级人工智能（ASI）跃迁。其对科学发现、宏观经济与人类社会结构的重塑烈度与传导速度，将远超 AGI 本身。为这一历史性范式转移做准备，亟需系统梳理从 AGI 通向 ASI 的技术路线图，并建立严谨可量化的评估观测体系。
为了科学剖析前沿 AI 的演化轨迹，将生物智能与人工机器智能视作同一连续谱系至关重要。人类水平的 AGI 仅是该智能演化光谱上的一个特定路标。
超级智能（ASI）位于连续谱系的更高阶：它是一种能够以更少算力资源和极短时间，在耗费人类顶级专家团队数年乃至数十年协同攻关的复合复杂任务中，持续且全方位压倒人类专家集群的高阶系统。例如在几周内完成整个科学领域原本需要数年的突破，或在芯片微架构研发上达成跨国科技巨头全年的研发产出。更为核心的是，ASI 必须在人类关切的几乎所有任务领域均达到此一基准，而非仅局限于狭义垂直领域。
在数学理论层面，我们对智能连续谱系的极值——即通用智能的理论物理与计算极限拥有坚实的理解。我们熟知算力、逻辑复杂度和物理维度的硬约束，诸如对气候混沌系统、人体复杂免疫机制及人类宏观经济行为的绝对预测上限。
然而知晓物理极限并不能回答通往极限之前的曲率。即便在理论推导中，准确预言一个“足够优秀”的工程近似智能能够迸发出何种效能亦极度困难。正如完美破解国际象棋的算力需求远超地球总和，但一块微缩芯片的工程启发式算法即可击败全人类大师。
我们唯一确证的是，根本性物理极限远在当今 AI 系统与人类智力之上。但在人类水平 AGI 与理论极限之间的广袤空间，即涵盖专家级 AGI 与各层级超级智能的庞大技术阶梯，目前仍是几乎完全未被涉足的处女地。
过去十年中，前沿 AI 能力的飞跃源自有效算力的指数级复合增长，由三大核心引擎持续驱动：硬件能效微架构跃升、算法大规模扩展，以及架构本身的突破。随着前沿 AI 从基础感知走向自主科学推理，自动化科研的正反馈闭环将从根本上决定迈向超级智能的时代时间线。
full_text:
As multiple technological routes toward artificial general superintelligence take shape, the regime beyond AGI is shifting from philosophical speculation to empirical research and governance questions.

For decades, AI research has been focused on a monumental milestone: building artificial general intelligence, or AGI — machines that match humans across nearly all cognitive tasks. It was always clear that, in principle, intelligence could progress beyond human level, but the prospect of AGI was far enough off, and surrounded by ample uncertainties of its own, that looking past it felt premature.

Now that AGI is coming within reach, we can no longer put off seriously considering what comes next. While far from certain, AI could continue to advance at its current pace — and possibly even accelerate — towards artificial general superintelligence, or ASI. It could have a profound impact on science, the economy, and society at a scale and speed much greater than AGI itself. Preparing for that potential shift requires mapping the possible roads from AGI to ASI and building rigorous, reliable ways to track progress.

To examine how the development of advanced AI might unfold, it helps to think of general intelligence, whether biological or artificial, as existing on a continuum. Human-level AGI is just one point along that spectrum.

ASI sits further along as an advanced system that consistently outperforms large groups of human experts on tasks that could take them years to complete, using fewer resources and less time. Examples would be making the same scientific progress as an entire research field in a fraction of the time, or achieving technological developments, such as in chip design, on par with what large companies can do in a year. ASI would need to meet this bar across virtually all tasks of human interest, not just some in narrow domains.

Interestingly, we have a good mathematical understanding of the very upper end of the intelligence continuum — the theoretical limits of general intelligence. We also know about hard physical, logical, and complexity-theoretic limits to what AI can achieve, such as predicting how real-world complex systems — from climate to immune systems to human societies — play out with arbitrary precision.

Yet knowing those upper limits doesn’t tell us what comes before them. Even in theory, it’s hard to predict how capable a ‘good enough’ approximation of general intelligence can be. For example, solving chess perfectly requires far more computing power than exists on Earth, yet a thumbnail-sized chip can play the game well enough to defeat any human.

What we do know is that fundamental limits lie far beyond both today’s AI systems and humans. But the vast space between human-level AI and theoretical limits to intelligence, which encompasses expert AGI and a whole regime of more and more advanced superintelligent systems, is largely uncharted.

Over the last ten years, AI progress was fueled by steady growth in effective compute, driven by three compounding factors: hardware efficiency, algorithmic scaling, and structural model improvements. As frontier AI moves from perception to autonomous scientific reasoning, the compounding feedback loops of automated research will fundamentally dictate the timeline toward superintelligence.

paragraphs_zh: 2023年1月，在 OpenAI 推出 ChatGPT 且全球掀起人工智能狂潮数月后，Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代伊收到了一封来自 Iconiq Capital 的引荐邮件。这家以管理超级富豪家族办公室起家的顶级投资机构，对这家初创公司展现出极高兴趣。

title: Sources: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving now to let the White House get a successor confirmed before Democrats take the Senate in January (Axios)
title_en: Sources: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving now to let the White House get a successor confirmed before Democrats take the Senate in January (Axios)

author: Axios
content_snippet:
White House national cyber director Sean Cairncross is leaving his post, Axios has learned.

Why it matters: Cairncross did not want to serve another two years and is leaving now to give the White House time to secure Senate confirmation before Democrats take control in January, two sources said.

The background: Cairncross leads the Office of the National Cyber Director, which coordinates cybersecurity policy and strategy across the federal government.

Case in point: He held technical meetings
summary_en: US National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is stepping down to provide a transition window for his successor to be confirmed by the Senate before Democrats gain control in January. As the head of the Office of the National Cyber Director, Cairncross led federal cybersecurity strategy and notably directed technical reviews of AI firms like Anthropic following commerce-led export control implementations.
